## MoodBuro 0.3.2

### Timetable in the AI assistant

- The assistant can now read the timetable weeks you saved in MoodBuro. Ask questions such as “What are my classes today, and where?” or “How long is my lunch break on Thursday?”. It answers with titles, Paris times, rooms and speakers.
- Sessions the answer relies on appear as cards under it, showing the day, times, room, and whether a session is remote or tentative. Choose a card to open that week in Agenda › Timetable with the session selected.
- Access is read-only: the assistant cannot add, change or remove timetable sessions. It is only offered for organisations with InspCal timetables, when you attach the organisation or a course and Moodle context sharing is on.
- Only saved weeks are known. If no saved week covers a day, the assistant says so rather than guessing. Questions are limited to 31 days at a time.

### Privacy

With Moodle context sharing on, the saved timetable sessions the assistant looks up (title, times, room and speakers) are now sent to your AI provider along with the other context. Settings → AI Assistant describes exactly what is shared. Turning sharing off still keeps all Moodle and timetable data on your Mac.

### Timetable reading

- Updated the InspCal engine to read the 16–20 November timetable: half-cohort headings, groups that wrap across lines, and the vote end-time rule.

### Install or upgrade

From MoodBuro 0.2.0 or later, check for updates in Settings → General. For a first installation or an earlier version, download the universal macOS DMG (Apple Silicon and Intel), verify it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`, quit MoodBuro, then drag the app into Applications.

The app is ad-hoc signed and not notarized. macOS may require first-launch approval in System Settings → Privacy & Security. macOS 12 is the configured minimum; full supported-platform, Intel runtime and installed update qualification remain in progress.

### Assets

- Universal `.dmg` installer
- Signed `.app.tar.gz` update archive and `.sig`
- `latest.json` stable update manifest for both Mac architectures
- `SHA256SUMS.txt`
